subject: Numeracy
title: Numerals 1 to 5 in order
objectives: Children will recognise the numerals 4 and 5 with support.
Children will place numeral cards 1 to 5 in order with help.
content: Meeting the numerals 4 and 5, matching numerals 1 to 5 to groups, and putting numeral cards in order.
teachingActivities: Show each new numeral large and trace it in the air; always pair a numeral with a group; make the number line from left to right as children say the numbers.
learnerActivities: Match numerals to groups to five, place cards in order, and play numeral and quantity games.
resources: A string or paper strip as a number line
assessment: Check numeral-to-group matching to five with support and ordering of numeral cards from one to five.
expectedOutcomes: Matches numerals 1 to 5 to groups with support.
Orders 1 to 3 independently and 1 to 5 with help.
crossCurricular: Literacy: left to right order and sequencing
Physical Development: carrying and placing cards

lessons.title: Meet four and five
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will recognise the numerals 4 and 5 and match them to groups of four and five.
successCriteria: Points to the numeral 4 or 5 when asked
Matches a numeral to a group
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can match numerals 1 to 3 to groups, count to five with support and trace numerals in sand.
resources: Dot cards for four and five
lessons.starter: Hold up four blocks and ask "How many?" Count them together. Show the numeral 4 and say "This is how we write four."
teacherActivities: Trace the numeral 4 in the air and say "Down, across, down." Place four blocks beside the card.
Do the same for the numeral 5 with five blocks. Say "Five. A straight line, a belly, a hat."
Mix the numeral cards 1 to 5 and ask a child to find the 4.
Show a dot card and ask "Which numeral?"
learnerActivities: Children trace in the air and count the blocks.
Children trace the numeral 5 and count five blocks.
Child points to the numeral 4 and says "four".
Children match the dot card to the numeral card.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Trace the numeral 4 in the air and say "Down, across, down." Place four blocks beside the card. Children: Children trace in the air and count the blocks.
Step 2. Teacher: Do the same for the numeral 5 with five blocks. Say "Five. A straight line, a belly, a hat." Children: Children trace the numeral 5 and count five blocks.
Step 3. Teacher: Mix the numeral cards 1 to 5 and ask a child to find the 4. Children: Child points to the numeral 4 and says "four".
Step 4. Teacher: Show a dot card and ask "Which numeral?" Children: Children match the dot card to the numeral card.

practical.title: Four and five match
steps: Give each pair numeral cards 4 and 5 and a basket of blocks.
One child takes a card; the partner counts out that number of blocks.
practical.safety: Use blocks larger than a child’s fist. Keep cards and blocks on the mat.

differentiation.support: Match numeral 4 only with a group of four lined up beside it.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find the numeral for a group chosen by a friend.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Can you show me the number 5?
How many blocks go with the number 4?

lessons.conclusion: Hold up the numeral 5 and five fingers. Say "Five!" and clap five times.
lessons.homeConnection: Find numbers four and five on a clock or a phone and say them.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "recognise the numerals 4 and 5 and match them to groups of four and five" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Putting numbers in order
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will put the numeral cards 1 to 3 in order and 1 to 5 with help.
successCriteria: Says the numbers as they place them
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can match numerals 1 to 3 to groups, count to five with support and trace numerals in sand.
resources: A string number line on the floor
lessons.starter: Show the cards in a jumble and say "Oh no, the numbers are mixed up! Can you help me put them in order?"
teacherActivities: Start the line by placing the numeral 1 at the left. Say "One goes first."
Ask a child to find the next numeral, 2. Place it beside the 1.
Continue to 3, then 4 and 5, with children placing each card.
Mix the cards and let pairs build the number line again.
learnerActivities: Children watch and say "one".
Child chooses the 2 and places it in the line.
Children place cards and say the numbers.
Pairs order the cards and check by counting.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Start the line by placing the numeral 1 at the left. Say "One goes first." Children: Children watch and say "one".
Step 2. Teacher: Ask a child to find the next numeral, 2. Place it beside the 1. Children: Child chooses the 2 and places it in the line.
Step 3. Teacher: Continue to 3, then 4 and 5, with children placing each card. Children: Children place cards and say the numbers.
Step 4. Teacher: Mix the cards and let pairs build the number line again. Children: Pairs order the cards and check by counting.

practical.title: Number line build
steps: Lay a string line on the floor.
Children take turns placing a numeral card in order.
They count along the line when finished.
practical.safety: Fix the string to the floor with tape so it does not trip anyone. Keep cards large and smooth.

differentiation.support: Order only 1, 2 and 3 with the cards already near the line.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find a missing number after you remove one card.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Can you put the cards in order?
questions.expected: Child places cards one to three or five in order.

lessons.conclusion: Point along the number line and count from one to five together.
lessons.homeConnection: Count along a row of items on the table or step on numbered stones.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "put the numeral cards 1 to 3 in order and 1 to 5 with help" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Which numeral, which group?
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will match numerals 1 to 5 to groups of objects.
successCriteria: Counts out the number shown on a numeral card
Matches a numeral to a group
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can match numerals 1 to 3 to groups, count to five with support and trace numerals in sand.
lessons.starter: Hold a numeral card behind your back and say "I am thinking of a number. It tells how many blocks to take." Reveal the card.
teacherActivities: Show the numeral 3 and count out three blocks into a tray.
Show the numeral 5 and let a child count out five blocks.
Show a tray with a group and ask "Which numeral matches?"
Play "numeral and tray": each child picks a card and fills a tray.
learnerActivities: Children count with you and check.
Child counts five blocks into a tray.
Children point to the matching numeral.
Child counts out blocks to match their numeral.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the numeral 3 and count out three blocks into a tray. Children: Children count with you and check.
Step 2. Teacher: Show the numeral 5 and let a child count out five blocks. Children: Child counts five blocks into a tray.
Step 3. Teacher: Show a tray with a group and ask "Which numeral matches?" Children: Children point to the matching numeral.
Step 4. Teacher: Play "numeral and tray": each child picks a card and fills a tray. Children: Child counts out blocks to match their numeral.

practical.title: Fill the tray
steps: A child picks a card and fills a tray with that many blocks.
practical.safety: Use blocks that are too large to swallow; sit on the floor mat; supervise all trays.

differentiation.support: Use only numerals 1 to 3 and place the blocks in a row beside the card.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to find two different numerals that make the same group when added by counting on.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Can you put four blocks in the tray?

expectedOutcomes: Counts out a group to match a numeral
Matches numerals 1 to 5 to groups with support
lessons.conclusion: Count each tray aloud and say "The numbers match."
lessons.homeConnection: Show your child a number and ask them to bring that many spoons.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "match numerals 1 to 5 to groups of objects" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Numeral line walk
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will walk along a floor number line saying the numbers from one to five.
successCriteria: Steps on each numeral and says the number
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can match numerals 1 to 3 to groups, count to five with support and trace numerals in sand.
resources: Numeral cards 1 to 5 taped to the floor in a line
lessons.starter: Beat the drum and say "A number path! Let us walk along it and say the numbers."
teacherActivities: Walk slowly along the line stepping on each card and saying the number.
Place a soft toy on a numeral and ask "Where is Teddy? On which number?"
Let a child be the caller while the others stand on the numeral.
learnerActivities: Children watch, then walk after you.
Children walk to the numeral called and stand on it.
Children say the number where the toy is.
Child calls a number and the group moves to it.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Walk slowly along the line stepping on each card and saying the number. Children: Children watch, then walk after you.
Step 2. Teacher: Call "Stand on 3!" and "Stand on 5!" Children: Children walk to the numeral called and stand on it.
Step 3. Teacher: Place a soft toy on a numeral and ask "Where is Teddy? On which number?" Children: Children say the number where the toy is.
Step 4. Teacher: Let a child be the caller while the others stand on the numeral. Children: Child calls a number and the group moves to it.

practical.title: Number path game
steps: Tape five numeral cards to the floor.
Children walk along them saying each number.
They stop at the numeral called by a friend.
practical.safety: Tape the cards securely and check the floor is dry; one child at a time on the line with an adult nearby.

differentiation.support: Use only three numerals and walk beside the child.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to walk backwards from five to one.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: What number are you standing on?
questions.expected: The numeral on the card under the child.

questions.question: Can you stand on number 4?
questions.expected: Child finds and stands on the numeral 4.

expectedOutcomes: Walks along a number line saying numbers
lessons.conclusion: Walk the line one last time saying "one, two, three, four, five" and sit down.
lessons.homeConnection: Draw numbers with chalk on the ground and hop along them with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "walk along a floor number line saying the numbers from one to five" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Numerals one to five stations
lessons.subject: Numeracy
objectives: Children will show they can recognise, order and match numerals 1 to 5 at three stations.
successCriteria: Matches numerals 1 to 5 to groups with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children can match numerals 1 to 3 to groups, count to five with support and trace numerals in sand.
lessons.starter: Sing the numeral song and show the three stations.
teacherActivities: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely.
Ask "Which numeral goes here?" and "What comes next?"
Record each child’s level and take photographs.
learnerActivities: Children play at each station.
Child answers by pointing or saying.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Rotate groups every four minutes and observe one station closely. Children: Children play at each station.
Step 2. Teacher: Ask "Which numeral goes here?" and "What comes next?" Children: Child answers by pointing or saying.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level and take photographs. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Station circuit
practical.safety: Remove small items; tape floor cards securely; supervise each station.

differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to lead the number path game.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: matches numerals 1 to 5 to groups; orders 1 to 3 independently and 1 to 5 with help.

questions.question: Which numeral matches these blocks?
questions.expected: The correct numeral, up to five.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 5
Recognises and orders numerals to five
lessons.conclusion: Sing the numeral song and tidy up together.
lessons.homeConnection: Count numbers on a phone keypad with your child.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "show they can recognise, order and match numerals 1 to 5 at three stations" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
